parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A photon has an energy of $3.11 \times 10^{-19} \text{J}$.

Calculate the momentum of the photon.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem: A laser beam has a power of $350 \text{mW}$. The light from the laser has a wavelength of $640 \text{nm}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Determine the number of photons emitted by the laser in a time of $1.0 \text{s}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The laser beam is incident normally on a surface that absorbs all of the photons.

Show that the force $F$ exerted on the surface by the laser beam is given by
$$F = \frac{P}{c}$$
where $P$ is the power of the laser beam and $c$ is the speed of light.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem:
Light of a single wavelength is incident on the surface of different metals. The work function energy of the metals is given in Table 7.1.

Table 7.1

| metal | work function energy/$\text{eV}$ |
| tungsten | 4.49 |
| magnesium | 3.68 |
| potassium | 2.26 |

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: For the metals in Table 7.1, calculate the value of the largest threshold wavelength.
